answers.text: The 3D neuron is a schematic teaching illustration. Dendrites are the branching inputs, the soma is the cell body, and myelin is shown around the axon. The calculation uses one membrane voltage for the entire neuron. Branch lengths and myelin do not affect its firing rate, and pulse transit is illustrative rather than a modeled conduction speed. [p.1–3, 3D demo teaching notes]

The model fires when membrane potential reaches −50 mV, then resets to −65 mV for a 2 ms refractory interval. A 1 nA input settles at −55 mV, so it never reaches threshold. Use 2 nA in lesson 3 to reproduce its 33-spike first-second target. [p.3, demo teaching notes]

A larger time constant slows the approach to equilibrium. The equilibrium is still Vrest + RI, so changing τ changes the pace, not that final subthreshold level. Compare 5 ms and 50 ms with I = 1 nA in lesson 2. [p.2, demo teaching notes]

The Python reference and browser use the same Euler timestep, 0.1 ms. The authored one-second reference runs yield 33 spikes at 2 nA and 63 at 3 nA. This verifies the demo implementation, not a biological fit or a published paper result. [p.4, demo teaching notes]
The model rests at −65 mV. With no input and voltage already at rest, the derivative is zero. Increase the input to see how the voltage shifts. [p.1–2, demo teaching notes]

other: This demo has stored answers about threshold, membrane voltage, time constant, and firing rate. Ask about one of those topics. For uploaded papers, the connected Tutor answers from the source pages.
